definitions.explanation: An official document acknowledging that payment has been received.

examples.japanese: {領収書|りょうしゅうしょ}をください。
examples.english: May I have a receipt, please?

examples.japanese: {経費|けいひ}{精算|せいさん}には{領収書|りょうしゅうしょ}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Receipts are needed for expense reimbursement.

examples.japanese: {領収書|りょうしゅうしょ}に{宛名|あてな}を{書|か}いてもらった。
examples.english: I had them write a name/address on the receipt.

notes:
{領収書|りょうしゅうしょ} is a compound: {領収|りょうしゅう} (receipt of payment) + {書|しょ} (document).

CONTRAST:
- {領収書|りょうしゅうしょ} (formal receipt, often for business expenses)
- レシート (cash register receipt, informal)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {領収書|りょうしゅうしょ}をもらう (to get a receipt)
- {領収書|りょうしゅうしょ}を{発行|はっこう}する (to issue a receipt)
- {領収書|りょうしゅうしょ}を{切|き}る (to write/issue a receipt)

JAPANESE RECEIPT FORMAT:
- {宛名|あてな} (recipient name - often 「上様」for anonymous)
- {金額|きんがく} (amount)
- {但|ただ}し{書|が}き (description of goods/services)
- {日付|ひづけ} (date)

CULTURAL NOTE:
「上様」(うえさま) is commonly written as recipient name when specific name isn't needed.
